name: Burg Heinfels
kurzbeschreibung: Burg Heinfels – Queen of the Pustertal: first documented in 1243, Görzer residence castle, tour from the keep to the bastions and museum.
beschreibung:
Overview

The monumental Burg Heinfels – reverently praised as the "Queen of the Pustertal" – perches on a steeply falling rocky spur at 1,130 metres above sea level high above the confluence of the Villgratental and the East Tyrolean Hochpustertal near Sillian. As one of the mightiest and most historic fortifications in the entire Alpine region, the fortress secured the vital trade route between Tirol and Venice for centuries. Following exemplary comprehensive renovations, the monument now shines in renewed glory and captivates visitors with interactive exhibition rooms, spectacular wall walks, and panoramic views of the Dolomites.

History & Architecture

According to legend, the stronghold was originally founded by the Huns; historically verified is its first documentary mention in 1243 in the possession of the powerful Bishops of Freising. In the late 13th century, the Grafen von Görz acquired the complex and expanded it into their most important stronghold in the Pustertal. Following the death of Count Leonhard in 1500, Heinfels passed to Emperor Maximilian I., who upgraded the castle into a modern territorial fortress with bold outworks and artillery bastions. In 1526 and during the Peasants' War, the fortress defied furious sieges. After severe fires and centuries of decay, the Museumsverein Burg Heinfels was founded in 2014: over a six-year construction period, the extensive castle grounds were renovated in accordance with heritage conservation guidelines for millions of euros and reopened in 2020 as a modern museum. The historic fabric encompasses three historic cores: the medieval upper castle with the prominent keep (Bergfried), the Gothic chapel quadrangle with frescoes, and the early modern bastions and gun towers.

Visit & Arrival

Burg Heinfels is open seasonally from early May to late October from Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00 (in July and August daily without a closing day; last admission 16:00). Visits can be made independently with a modern audio guide (in multiple languages) or as part of guided tours. Admission prices (as of 2025/2026): Adults approx. €11.00, seniors and students €9.50, children (6–14 years) €6.00, family ticket approx. €26.00. With the regional Osttirol Card, admission is free. Arrival by train: Drautalbahn (ÖBB) to Bahnhof Sillian or Bahnhof Heinfels, from where a signposted panoramic hiking trail leads up to the castle gate in about 20 minutes on foot. By car: B100 Drautalstraße to Heinfels, turn off towards the castle; visitor parking is available at the foot of the castle hill by the municipal office/sports grounds.

Tips

The walk up to the castle covers around 60 metres in altitude on an asphalt path; the castle courtyard and dining area are accessible with few barriers, while the ascent to the historic keep is via stairs. The view from the battlement wall over the Lienzer and Sextener Dolomites is exceptionally worthwhile. Combine your excursion with a visit to the nearby Punbrugge – Austria's longest historic wooden bridge dating from 1781.
oeffnungszeiten: Mai bis Oktober Di–So 10:00–17:00 Uhr (Juli/Aug täglich)
